decision_titles: Indigenous Peoples Day proclamation at October 6 Council meeting
plain_text:
Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee  
September 14, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
Present: Anne, Lauren, Ariane, Flo, Breese, Jamie, Aiden (remote), Guest: Scott Whiting 
from the Charter Revision Commission 
Absent: David, Syed 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order at 5:33 PM. 
 
2. Public Comment 
No members of the public were present. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
3.a. August 10, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
Motion by Jamie, seconded by Anne, to approve the August 10, 2026 meeting minutes. 
Vote: Unanimous 
 
3.b. September 1, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
Motion by Anne, seconded by Ariane, to approve the September 1, 2026 meeting 
minutes. 
Vote: Unanimous 
 
4. Special Guest 
4.a City Charter Discussion with Scott Whiting, Charter Revision Commissioner 
Scott Whiting, member of the Charter Review Commission, shared information with the 
Committee about the Charter Commission.
The City Charter is only about 20 pages but has significant influence on what the 
structure of government is and how the City operates. It was last reviewed in 2016 and 
voters recently approved creating a Charter Revision Commission to review it again. The 
Commission’s goal isn’t to reinvent the wheel but to focus on what areas need to be 
updated to reflect the times we live in. 
There are 9 members of the Commission – one elected member per Ward and two 
additional members appointed by the Mayor. So far, the commission has mostly had 
organizational meetings and a public comment session. Tonight’s meeting is just the 
second meeting where they will be getting into the language of the charter and beginning 
discussions on potential revisions. Everything that is approved by the Commission will 
ultimately go out to the public to be voted on as referendum questions. The 
Commission must have a draft of proposed changes to the Council no later than May or 
June of next year. 
Members of the public can attend any Charter Revision Commission meeting and share 
input. There is one public comment period scheduled at the beginning of the meeting 
and they are considering adding a second one at the end. Meetings will mostly be on 
Mondays with some Thursday meetings. 
Anne would like to know if there is anything that could be controversial from a DEI 
perspective so that we can be involved. 
Jamie watched the first meeting and appreciated that there was strong support for 
public comment.  
Lauren asked if there is another planned meeting devoted specifically to public 
comment. Scott said that there isn’t, but there is nothing prohibited from sharing 
general thoughts at any upcoming meetings. He also encouraged calling and emailing 
members. 
Flo asked how the Commission is ensuring that as many people as possible who want to 
participate have the opportunity to. Scott said that the Commission is trying to utilize as 
many means of communication as possible.  
Anne is concerned about some cities that have made biological gender a contingency 
for using public restrooms. Scott does not see that as being within the scope of the 
charter but would not support it if such a conversation was proposed. 
Lauren asked if there is a possibility to have a discussion about the City Charter in 
another forum, such as the library. Flo suggested getting materials translated into other 
languages.
Flo asked about Charter changes with budgetary implications, as she believes that the 
Council and Mayor’s pay is too low and that impacts who can participate in the 
governmental process. Scott believes that elected official compensation is the only 
area that would have budget implications, and he agreed that people who want to serve 
should be paid in a way that compensates them for their time appropriately so that they 
can be fully engaged. 
 
5. Current Events 
5.a Member Check-In 
Members shared how the past month has gone for them. 
Lauren shared information about the free vet clinic at McArthur Library that she 
volunteered at this weekend. Some Committee members expressed interest in having 
the Committee support future sessions of this event. 
Breese shared that tonight will be the last meeting with the Committee. Members 
thanked him for his contributions. 
Flo announced that she had a call with the Mayor this morning and also resigned. Her 
last meeting will be in October. She emphasized the challenges of the Committee’s 
work being met with resistance and how that impacted her decision to end her term 
early. The Mayor asked Flo what he can do and she suggested that he attend a meeting 
to show the Committee that they are heard. 
 
6. Discussion Items 
6.a Indigenous Peoples' Day Proclamation 
Motion by Breese, seconded by Lauren, to recommend that the Mayor read the 
Indigenous Peoples Day Proclamation at the October 6 City Council meeting. 
Vote: Unanimous 
 
6.b Diversity Calendar Review - Upcoming Observances 
Danica provided the Diversity calendar for October through December. Flo confirmed 
that we are scheduled to prepare proclamations for Homelessness Awareness Month 
and for the December holidays.
Jamie volunteered to prepare the Homelessness Awareness Month proclamation. Anne 
will send an email to Vassie with last year’s proclamation and ask for current data about 
how many people Seeds serves. Flo also suggested referencing the benefit event that 
will be held on November 7. The proclamation would be voted on at the October 
Committee meeting and recommended to be read at the November 3 City Council 
meeting. 
Ariane volunteered to write the December holidays proclamation. Danica will send her a 
copy of the previous year’s proclamation. 
 
6.c Review of Expiring Terms and Recruitment/Succession Planning Discussion 
Members reviewed their term expiration dates. Danica shared an overview of the 
reappointment process. 
Given current and anticipated vacancies, Anne asked if we could reach out to those who 
applied last time and were not able to be seated.  
Danica shared that we will need to appoint a new chair after the October meeting.  
 
6.d October Meeting Date 
The next meeting will be held on October 19 at 5:30 PM due to the Indigenous Peoples 
Day holiday. Lauren noted she will attend virtually. Aiden may not be available. 
 
7. Other Business 
Flo thanked Anne for drafting the Hispanic Heritage Month proclamation, as well as those 
who moved their schedules around to vote during the emergency meeting. 
The Mayor’s edits to the submitted proclamation removed language related to Johan 
Sebastián Durán Guerrero and current events in Biddeford. Flo had a call with Mayor 
LaFountain and expressed that she did not want the proclamation to be communicated as 
being from the DEI Committee because of the extent of the edits that were made. The 
Mayor assured Flo that it would not be attributed to the Committee. Mayor LaFountain 
communicated to Anne after the agenda was published that he removed Johan’s name 
because his family had not been consulted. Committee members expressed that they felt 
their time invested into the proclamation was not respected and that they want to be a 
resource that is more utilized by the City.
Jamie would like us to reach out to other Committees to connect with them. 
 
8. Second Public Comment 
There were no members of the public present. 
 
9. Adjourn 
Meeting adjourned at 7:00 PM.
